# Assets: Configure Assets

Area overview and notes: [assets.md](../assets.md)

`POST /assets` · tenant-scoped token

Creates up to 500 assets in a single request. Elements are processed independently: a failing element does not block or roll back the others, and the response returns one result per submitted element in the order submitted, each carrying its own `status`. The stablecoin/SEMP tag can only be set here, on creation, and cannot be changed by a later update.

**Request body** (required, JSON)

An array of objects with these fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[].name` | string | Yes | The name of the asset. Must be unique among your configured assets, compared without regard to capitalization. The capitalization supplied is the capitalization stored and returned. At most 255 characters. |
| `[].type` | string | Yes | The class of asset. Transaction and inventory payloads publish the same values in title case (`Crypto`, `Fiat`, `Precious Metal`). One of: `CRYPTO`, `FIAT`, `PRECIOUS_METAL`. |
| `[].codes` | array of string | Yes | The codes that may be sent as `asset.code` on transactions for this asset. Each must be unique among your configured assets, compared without regard to capitalization, and at most 64 characters. The capitalization supplied is the capitalization stored and returned. At least one is required. |
| `[].is_stablecoin_or_semp` | boolean | No | Whether this asset is a stablecoin or SEMP (Specified Electronic Money Product). Taxbit derives the reporting jurisdictions for a tagged asset from a maintained list of codes rather than accepting them directly; see `stablecoin_reporting_jurisdictions`. Can only be set on creation, and `true` is accepted only when `type` is `CRYPTO`. On a response it is `true` for a tagged asset and omitted otherwise, the same way `dtif_code` and `qualification_status` are omitted when they do not apply. |

**Response 200**: One result per submitted element, in the order submitted. Elements can fail individually while others succeed, so inspect each element's `status` field rather than the HTTP status code.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | array of value | Yes | One result per submitted asset, in the order they were submitted. A failed element also carries `index`, its zero-based position in the request, so it can be tied back to the asset that produced it. Note that this envelope differs from `POST /v1/form-items/batch`, which groups its outcomes into separate `successes` and `failures` arrays instead of preserving submission order in one list. |

**Errors:** 400 The request body is not an array of 1 to 500 elements. Failures of individual elements do not use this status. They are reported per element in the 200 response. · 401 Unauthorized · 403 Forbidden · 409 A concurrent request configured an asset with the same name or code. Retrying the request reports the specific conflict on the affected element. Conflicts detected during normal processing do not use this status. They are reported per element in the 200 response. · 429 Too Many Requests
